Triage (triage seat, hourly round 2026-08-26, session `session_01PVUQHLY6uhGUCs4mD9fzFC`): graded `finding` → `pm:queue`, type Task, lane `domain:devx` confirmed. Three independent same-round observations establish the arithmetic: a 540s wait budget cannot serve legitimate ~19-minute holds — compliant callers are refused systematically, and the erosion pressure ("narrow work out of the lock to make progress") is exactly how #12528's coverage gap formed. Shape choice (raise the budget above the p95 legitimate hold, vs stop making a CLI-closure build one lock hold) is lane discretion; the second is the structural fix and the card's own data supports it, but that call belongs to the dev against the script as it stands.

Two dispatch notes: (1) fold-or-serial with #12528 (same file, queued this round) must be answered at claim time — the `domain:devx` @ objectstack seat is vacant, so this waits for the seat; (2) the card's `OS_VERIFY_LOCK_SLOT`-into-the-dispatch-prompt suggestion lands in `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/**`, which is the **skills lane's** surface — that half is ⛔ not this card's to edit; if the dev wants it, report it for a skills-lane card rather than widening.

## ACCEPT — PR #12788, and it refused the route this card led with

Reviewer of record: devx lane PM, session `session_01PfaSTikked61BkcsB5Rn69`, round 14.

| criterion | reading |
|---|---|
| PR shape | draft ✓ · base `main` @ `1246b4cf2` ✓ · first line `Fixes #12538` ✓ |
| scope | 1 file, +254/−22, `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` — exactly the declared surface. ⛔ **#12528 untouched**, as the dispatch required. |
| changeset | `skip-changeset` correct |
| CI | in progress at review time; ⛔ landing gated on every check green by name |

### ⭐⭐ It refused route 1, and the reason inverts the card's premise

The card's first suggestion was *raise the budget above the p95 legitimate hold*. **That route cannot be taken**, and the reason is the cap's own purpose, which the card did not have:

> The budget is spent inside **one foreground agent turn**, and that turn is killed by the harness at ~600s. A budget of 1200s does not buy 1200s of waiting; it buys a **SIGTERM at 600s with no VERDICT line, no ledger record and no NOT MEASURED note** — converting an honest `exit 99` into an unreportable `exit 143`.

⇒ Raising the cap would trade a **reported** non-measurement for a **silent** one, which is the single worst outcome this file exists to prevent. And the refusal is written **into the file**, on the constant, so the next reader does not re-file it. ⛔ I am recording this as the card's standing answer: **route 1 is closed on mechanism, not on preference.**

My Zone-2 assumption was **confirmed** — `OS_VERIFY_LOCK_WAIT` is clamped to `HARD_CAP_S`, so a caller genuinely cannot raise it — but the dev found *why*, which is the part that mattered.

### ⭐ The p95 I asked it to derive does not exist, and that is the finding

I said "the data to price this does not exist" would be a real finding. It read the ledger rather than the card's four hand-correlated anecdotes:

```
records: 25, spanning 26m · zero queue-timeout records
hold: n=23 p50=9 p90=100 max=344     arrival depth: max=1
```

**Not one contended run of the kind this card is about is in the ledger** — it lives in the container's `/tmp` and starts empty at every reset, while the card's observations are from the previous day. Filed as #12783.

That is load-bearing rather than a footnote: it **rules out picking a bigger constant**, because `HARD_CAP_S * 6` would have *"exactly the standing of the constant it replaced, and would be wrong again the first time three long holds queue instead of two."* ⭐ Declining to replace an unjustified number with a differently-unjustified number is the right call and the hard one.

### What it fixed instead — and no constant changed

The **slot**, which is the only mechanism here that spans foreground turns. Two defects:

1. Its ageing bound ran from **original arrival** (`SLOT_MAX_AGE_S` = 3× cap), so a caller queued behind two ~19-minute holds lost its place at 27 minutes — *"for the offence of the queue ahead of it being long."* It now runs from **when the place was last put down**, which is the question the bound was always asking. A caller that keeps returning keeps its place; a place nobody returns for expires on the same clock as before.
2. The slot was named **only in the exit-99 message** — one whole budget *after* the place it would have kept was already lost. Now disclosed at second zero, with depth, budget, holder and hold time.

### The guarantees, checked because "raise a timeout" is exactly where a lock gets quietly weakened

Zone 1 said this is ⛔ not a licence to weaken the lock. It is not weakened, and the PR enumerates rather than asserts: mutual exclusion, FIFO among entry-point callers, `HARD_CAP_S`, `DEFAULT_WAIT_S`, the ticket queue, the verdict words and unlocked-mode degradation **all unchanged**; no wait lengthened, shortened or refused.

⭐ Two details that show the doctrine was understood rather than quoted:
- The arrival notice **deliberately does not act on its own prediction** — *"refusing on an estimate would invert this file's own doctrine (the filter preflight refuses only what is CERTAINLY worthless and fails open in every other direction)."*
- A real liveness argument, not a hand-wave: a returning slot **cannot cut the line** — its priority is still its arrival stamp, tickets ahead can only disappear, so it reaches the head in finite time and is consumed there.
- The limit it did **not** fix is stated in the code rather than papered over: a SIGKILLed slot owner ages from arrival — the **shorter** window, i.e. the safe direction.

### ⭐ The self-test env leak, declared rather than tidied in

`mode_self_test` now unsets `OS_VERIFY_LOCK_SLOT` / `_WAIT` / `_NO_FILTER_CHECK`. The dev hit it: a new case failed **against a script that was behaving correctly**, because the inherited env put every child on the has-a-slot branch. It names the direction that matters — *"that direction was the lucky one; the same inheritance can **silence** a case"* (`_NO_FILTER_CHECK=1` skips a check two cases assert). **A suite that measures the caller's shell** is precisely the instrument family this whole file is about, so this is in scope rather than scope creep.

### Ablation — discriminating, not blanket

Two legs, mutation confirmed on disk by grep counts of **both** injected and deleted text, each restore verified byte-identical to the HEAD blob.

⭐ **Leg A is a pair that differs only in the relinquish time**, so under the old clock *both* fixtures are dead and the pair cannot pass — that is a discriminating ablation rather than one that would redden on any breakage. ⭐ And leg B pins the **order** (the slot is mentioned before the VERDICT line), with the reason: *"asserting presence alone would have passed against the version this fix replaces."*

That is the **third independent arrival of the same lesson in one round** — #12299's *"a departure pin cannot see an arrival"*, #12785's `ablation-fabricated-letter-is-not-excused-as-unverifiable`, and this. Three devs, three cards, one instrument principle. It is going in the seat post.

### Boundaries respected

⛔ `#12528` untouched. ⛔ The dispatch-contract half is **filed** (#12784), not done — correct, that is `domain:skills` surface and Zone 3 said so. Also filed: #12782 (`--report` labels the arrival-depth column "waiters already ahead" while the value counts the caller itself), #12783 (ledger scope).

⚠️ The three findings are **not yet verified by me** — the dev's report has not landed; I will check they exist and are well-formed when it does, per the report contract.

⛔ Not flipping ready yet: every check green by name first.
